name: LFMS pattern (500 Hz trains, McLean timing)
origin: McLean Hospital / Harvard Medical School (Rohan, Cohen); multisite trial led by Massachusetts General Hospital (Fava)
summary: The timing of low-field magnetic stimulation (LFMS), tested at McLean Hospital for rapid mood effects in depression: 500 Hz alternating pulses in 0.5-s trains every 2 s for 20 min, on all eight ring coils in phase. The original gradient coil gave under 2 mT, about 0.75 mT at the head surface, and a uniform induced electric field of about 0.7 V/m. This helmet gives at most 0.2 mT at the scalp and cannot produce the uniform electric field.
notes: Rohan 2014 give ramps of 256 us and dwell times of 768 us, 1.024 ms per half-wave or about 488 Hz (p.3), with 512 per train (Rohan 2004 p.3): a 0.524-s train. Fava 2018 round this to 1-ms trapezoids at 500 Hz in 0.5-s trains every 2 s for 20 min (l.162). The defining property is the induced electric field: 0.5 to 0.72 V/m in 256-us pulses, uniform to 5% across the head (Rohan 2004 p.3 [95]; Rohan 2014 p.3). The coil 'is designed to deliver the target fields at the end of the device, not in its center' (Rohan 2014 p.3). This program plays Fava's rounded timing on all eight ring coils in phase: each half-wave is two 0.5-ms steps at full scale, 600 trains per session. The ramps are lost and the edges are square; the 0.5-ms step cannot do better. Eight coils round the head do not stand in for the gradient coil: the helmet gives a few mV/m for microseconds under each coil and cannot make the electric field uniform. The original field was under 20 G (2 mT) in the device and about 7.5 G (0.75 mT) at the head surface (Rohan 2014 p.3, Fig. 1), and under 10 G in the brain (Rohan 2004 p.3 [95]); Fava 2018's figure of under 50 G is an upper bound (l.162). This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. Place for place, at its maximum the helmet gives 0.2 mT at the head surface, 3.8 times less, and 8.4 uT at 20 mm, up to 120 times less. Rohan 2014 reported mood gains only in combined secondary analyses, the Fava 2018 multisite trial was null, Dubin 2019 saw a benefit only after the third session, and a 2026 meta-analysis of 9 trials found a pooled benefit but rated its certainty low. No data exist for this pattern at this helmet's strength. Not a depression treatment: do not change medication or treatment because of it. The coils may click or whine at 500 Hz; the original sham reproduced the coil sound, so mask the sound in both arms of a blinded comparison. Not for people with epilepsy; stop on headache or distress.
setting: Lie flat or reclined with eyes closed in a quiet room (in the trials people lay supine with the top of the head, up to the eyebrows, inside the coil).
schedule: Original schedules: one 20-min session (Rohan 2014); three sessions 48 h apart (Dubin 2019); 20 min a day on 4 consecutive days (Fava 2018); twice daily for 2 weeks at home (Wu 2026).
source: Fava et al. 2018, Brain Stimul (LFMS waveform and multisite trial) https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5729080/ ; Rohan et al. 2014, Biol Psychiatry 76:186 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24331545/ ; Rohan et al. 2004, Am J Psychiatry 161:93 (MRI-based stimulator) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/14702256/ ; Dubin et al. 2019, J Affect Disord https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6486658/ ; Wu et al. 2026, J Affect Disord https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42203049/ ; Bharadwaj et al. 2026, meta-analysis https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41911470/
